title: How does a billed party lodge a dispute on a demurrage and detention invoice line?
content:
## Scope

Under the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category, a billed party who contests an invoice line of a per-container record lodges the dispute itself. This entry covers when that applies and the customer's own tool for lodging it.

## When it applies

1. A billed party disputing a demurrage invoice line on the ground rate_misapplied or free_time_misapplied lodges the dispute itself.
2. A withdrawn dispute does not count toward the one dispute an invoice line may carry, so a line whose only earlier dispute was withdrawn may be disputed again within the dispute window.

## Business effect of lodging

- One dispute is registered on the single invoice line, with the ground and the amount disputed, marked as submitted and stamped with the current time; it then waits for the desk's decision.
- Nothing is booked on the account by lodging.
- The customer then sees the dispute as submitted.

## How it is invoked

The tool is **lodge_dnd_dispute_1c3d36b3**. It is the customer's own tool: it must first be unlocked (unlock, through unlock_user_discoverable_tool) and handed over, to be run by the customer themselves.

## Parameters

- **dnd_id**: reference number of the free-time record whose invoice line is disputed, as given to the customer by the desk from the free-time record lookup.
- **invoice_event_id**: invoice reference of the single invoice line disputed, as given to the customer by the desk from the account entry lookup.
- **dispute_ground**: the ground of the dispute; the allowed values are exactly:
  - invoice_issued_late: the line was issued after the invoicing deadline;
  - rate_misapplied: the day rates or the rate class billed are wrong;
  - free_time_misapplied: the free days or the day count billed are wrong;
  - incorrect_event_dates: the recorded movement dates themselves are contested;
  - carrier_caused_delay: the days are blamed on a delay caused by the line;
  - terminal_closure: the days are blamed on a closure of the terminal.
- **disputed_amount_usd**: the part of the invoice line disputed, in USD, a positive figure given to 2 decimal places.

## Return

A successful lodging answers "Dispute (dispute reference) lodged on invoice line (invoice reference) of record (record reference): ground (ground), USD (amount) disputed, status submitted." The dispute reference is the identifier the desk quotes when it decides the dispute. An answer starting with "Error:" means no record exists under that reference and nothing was lodged.

## Points of judgement

**Q: The customer withdrew an earlier dispute on the same line. Can the line be disputed again?**
A: Yes, within the dispute window, because a withdrawn dispute does not count toward the one dispute a line may carry.

**Q: Who runs the tool?**
A: The customer themselves, once the desk has unlocked it and handed it over.
